qs.stem:
Statement: U ≤ H = V ≤ Y ≥ S; S = Q ≥ L
Conclusions:
I. V > Q
II. Y ≥ V
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: V and Q are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives Y ≥ V ⇒ true.

qs.stem:
Statement: I > R ≥ N ≥ Y ≥ O = J < X ≤ H
Conclusions:
I. N = Y
II. N > Y
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: N ≥ Y from the chain, so neither 'N = Y' nor 'N > Y' is definite alone, but together they cover '≥' ⇒ either.

qs.stem:
Statement: A ≤ S ≤ C ≥ I > U; Z = R > N ≥ U
Conclusions:
I. U < N
II. S ≤ R
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: chain gives only U ≤ N, not < ⇒ false.
II: S and R are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.

qs.stem:
Statement: V = D ≥ M ≥ Z; O < U > Z
Conclusions:
I. V ≥ M
II. Z < D
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: chain gives V ≥ M ⇒ true.
II: chain gives only Z ≤ D, not < ⇒ false.

qs.stem:
Statement: C > Q > D ≤ M ≤ I > N
Conclusions:
I. M ≥ N
II. I ≥ M
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: M and N are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives I ≥ M ⇒ true.

'every rain rice grows' is coded as 'fl nn wm dh'
'green rice season joy' is coded as 'mw nn wg dv'

qs.stem: What is the code for 'green'?
sol: 'green' appears in sentences [1, 4]; the only code common to exactly those sentences is 'dv'.

qs.stem: What does the code 'nn' stand for?
sol: 'nn' appears exactly in the sentences containing 'rice'.

qs.stem: What may be the possible code for 'every season'?
sol: 'every' is either 'fl' or 'dh' (it always appears together with 'grows'); 'season' = 'mw'. Only 'fl mw' is consistent among the options.

qs.stem: If 'every power' is coded as 'ag fl', then what is the code for 'grows'?
sol: 'every' and 'grows' share the codes 'fl'/'dh'. The new sentence shows 'every' = 'fl', so 'grows' = 'dh'.

qs.stem: How many words' codes can be definitely determined from the given information?
sol: Words whose sentence-pattern is unique: brings, green, joy, rain, rice, season ⇒ 6.

sol: 'gives' and 'high' share the codes 'vo'/'us'. The new sentence shows 'gives' = 'vo', so 'high' = 'us'.

qs.stem: How many words' codes can be definitely determined from the given information?
sol: Words whose sentence-pattern is unique: account, digital, loan, now, rate ⇒ 5.

Statement: R ≤ T = N = A = S > Z
Conclusions:
I. N > R
II. A = T
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: chain gives only N ≥ R, not > ⇒ false.
II: chain gives A = T ⇒ true.

qs.stem:
Statement: H > X > N = F; K > B ≥ Y < F
Conclusions:
I. Y < F
II. X < B
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: chain gives Y < F ⇒ true.
II: X and B are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.

sol: I: P and N are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives W < N ⇒ true.

sol: I: chain gives G < F ⇒ true.

'digital money high safe' is coded as 'ww pb ie ka'

qs.stem: What is the code for 'rate'?
sol: 'rate' appears in sentences [1, 3]; the only code common to exactly those sentences is 'ab'.

qs.stem: What does the code 'ku' stand for?
sol: 'ku' appears exactly in the sentences containing 'now'.

qs.stem: What may be the possible code for 'high safe'?
sol: 'high' is either 'ww' or 'ka' (it always appears together with 'money'); 'safe' = 'pb'. Only 'ww pb' is consistent among the options.

qs.stem: If 'high power' is coded as 'cu ww', then what is the code for 'money'?
sol: 'high' and 'money' share the codes 'ww'/'ka'. The new sentence shows 'high' = 'ww', so 'money' = 'ka'.

qs.stem: How many words' codes can be definitely determined from the given information?
sol: Words whose sentence-pattern is unique: account, digital, now, open, rate, safe ⇒ 6.

blocks.directions: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.
blocks.intro:
In a certain code language,
'green farmer crop brings' is coded as 'ut mm md af'
'green every rice season' is coded as 'iu nf oy ut'
'rice joy new brings' is coded as 'cr iu af wb'
'rice green every crop' is coded as 'iu ut oy mm'

qs.stem: What is the code for 'rice'?
sol: 'rice' appears in sentences [2, 3, 4]; the only code common to exactly those sentences is 'iu'.

qs.stem: What does the code 'nf' stand for?
sol: 'nf' appears exactly in the sentences containing 'season'.

qs.stem: What may be the possible code for 'joy brings'?
sol: 'joy' is either 'wb' or 'cr' (it always appears together with 'new'); 'brings' = 'af'. Only 'wb af' is consistent among the options.

qs.stem: If 'joy peace' is coded as 'wc wb', then what is the code for 'new'?
sol: 'joy' and 'new' share the codes 'wb'/'cr'. The new sentence shows 'joy' = 'wb', so 'new' = 'cr'.

qs.stem: How many words' codes can be definitely determined from the given information?
sol: Words whose sentence-pattern is unique: brings, crop, every, farmer, green, rice, season ⇒ 7.

qs.stem:
Statement: R > V < P; P > S = K < T < H
Conclusions:
I. R > V
II. H ≤ R
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: chain gives R > V ⇒ true.
II: H and R are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.

qs.stem:
Statement: G > I > W ≤ L < M; F ≤ K ≥ M
Conclusions:
I. F ≤ I
II. M > W
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: F and I are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives M > W ⇒ true.

qs.stem:
Statement: P > D ≥ Y ≥ U ≤ O > Z > V ≥ G
Conclusions:
I. D ≥ O
II. P > D
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: D and O are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives P > D ⇒ true.

qs.stem:
Statement: N ≥ T = E; E < A ≤ G = P ≤ K ≥ L
Conclusions:
I. G < N
II. P < K
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: I: G and N are not connected by a one-directional chain ⇒ false.
II: chain gives only P ≤ K, not < ⇒ false.

qs.stem:
Statement: M ≥ K ≤ X < E < Y; Y < O > L ≤ A ≤ P
Conclusions:
I. L < P
II. L = P
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
sol: L ≤ P from the chain, so neither 'L < P' nor 'L = P' is definite alone, but together they cover '≤' ⇒ either.
